A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Self-Feedback Training (SFT) work. Their main texts and supplementary Sections 6–11 are readable and support comparison of methods, experiments, figures, tables, and proofs despite pagination and citation changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-data experiments, SFT evaluations on five domain-generalization benchmarks, component ablations, and an algorithm timing comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds an OfficeHome analysis comparing SFT and SAM sharpness.

M1.justification: The two-phase SFT procedure, landscape refiner, projection cross-entropy objective, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 line renumbering and added notation explanations do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic three-class, four-domain dataset and VLCS, PACS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, and DomainNet. The new sharpness analysis uses existing OfficeHome coverage.

E2.justification: The SAM+SWAD comparator reported in v1 Table 4 is removed. ERM+SWAD is retained under the shorter name SWAD in v2 appendix Table 13, with identical scores. Comparator membership in the main benchmark and SAM-variant tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a diagnostic reporting sharpness separately for OfficeHome's Clipart, Product, and Real World domains and their maximum-minus-minimum range alongside accuracy (Figure 4). Existing splits, backbone configurations, tuning procedures, and hyperparameter searches remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 4.3 and Figure 4 examine whether SFT reduces domain-specific sharpness and its cross-domain variation. The SWAD-combination analysis is removed, while the toy landscape visualizations, sensitivity analysis, and component ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The existing three-run benchmark reporting, means and standard deviations, and 1000-run timing comparison are retained. Figure 4 introduces no new uncertainty estimates, seed information, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds OfficeHome sharpness measurements showing lower values and a smaller cross-domain range for SFT than SAM. v1's SAM+SWAD and SFT+SWAD result rows, averaging 85.8% and 86.5%, are removed. Tables 1–3 and matched appendix scores remain unchanged; SWAD's 85.1% result is relocated.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, PAC-Bayesian theorem and proof in Section 6, and KL-projection derivation and Proposition 3 in Section 7 are unchanged. Spelling out KL divergence and clarifying the label notation add explanation rather than new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about label-based landscape refinement, consistent flat minima, and improved domain generalization. The reported average gains over SAM remain 2.6 percentage points with ResNet-50 and 1.5 with ViT-B/16.

C2.justification: v2 interprets its new sharpness measurements as supporting the beneficial relationship between landscape consistency and generalization. It removes v1's qualification that direct comparison with SWAD is unfair because weight averaging uses a different model-selection approach.

D1.justification: v2 deletes promises to release code, logs, optimal hyperparameters, and model parameters from the abstract and Section 10. Hardware, synthetic-data generation details, and hyperparameter search spaces remain unchanged. Neither PDF provides a repository address, so this establishes removal of release commitments, not withdrawal of accessible resources.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a short discussion citing three efficient SAM works by Du et al., Ji et al., and Jiang et al. The bibliography also drops 35 entries unused in v1's text. The central positioning relative to existing domain-generalization and flat-minimum methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits include brief notation explanations, grammatical corrections, a corresponding-author marker, and revised bibliography formatting. The sharpness-analysis subsection replaces the weight-averaging discussion, and the ablation subsection is renumbered; the broader narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 4, removes the dedicated SWAD comparison table, and incorporates its retained SWAD baseline row into the appendix OfficeHome table. Subsequent tables are renumbered, with localized reflow of text and tables within the existing two-column layout.

improvement.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 4 add useful real-data evidence for the central consistency mechanism beyond v1's toy visualizations and accuracy ablations. This modest gain is partly offset by losing the SWAD-combination controls, although the SWAD baseline and main findings remain. Concrete implementation details are retained; the deleted release promises had not supplied actual code access.
